title: Quantum Channel Stein Theorem beyond Definite Causal Order
abstract: Distinguishability is a central concept in information theory and extends naturally to quantum systems. This work shows that, for any two finite-dimensional memoryless quantum channels, parallel, adaptive and general testing strategies achieve the same Stein exponent at every fixed type-I error tolerance $ε\in(0,1)$, namely the regularized channel relative entropy. When this rate is finite, any larger type-II exponent forces the probability of correctly accepting the null hypothesis to decay exponentially. Thus, adaptivity provides no asymptotic advantage. The key step is proving the continuity of the regularized sandwiched Rényi channel divergence at order one. We also derive the exact strong-converse exponent for general testers.
summary: This work establishes a quantum channel Stein theorem proving that the asymptotic rate for distinguishing between two quantum channels is independent of the testing strategy used (parallel, adaptive, or general). The key finding is that adaptivity offers no asymptotic advantage in this context. The paper rigorously connects hypothesis testing bounds to fundamental quantum divergences.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether different quantum channel testing strategies (parallel, adaptive, general/indefinite causal order) yield different asymptotic advantages when distinguishing between two quantum channels.
main_result: It proves that for any fixed error tolerance, all testing strategies achieve the same asymptotic rate, which is the regularized channel relative entropy, demonstrating that adaptivity provides no asymptotic advantage.
method: The analysis uses hypothesis testing theory, relating the achievable rate to the regularized channel relative entropy via continuity proofs of the sandwiched Rényi divergence.
model_or_system: The system involves finite-dimensional memoryless quantum channels, modeled as Completely Positive Trace-Preserving (CPTP) maps, $N$ and $M$. The testing is performed over $n$ uses of these channels.
key_observables: The asymptotic testing rate, $D_{\infty}(N \parallel M)$, and the error probabilities associated with the three tester types (parallel, adaptive, general).
important_parameters: The fixed type-I error tolerance $\epsilon \in (0, 1)$ and the number of uses $n 	o \infty$.
main_assumptions: The proof relies on establishing the continuity of the regularized sandwiched Rényi channel divergence at order one, and using the fixed-marginal de Finetti theorem for the general tester bound.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the asymptotic equality of testing rates across different strategies (Stein Theorem), to deriving exact one-shot duality relations, and finally establishing the exact strong-converse exponent based on these results.
why_interesting: It provides fundamental theoretical bounds on quantum channel discrimination, showing that complex causal structures (like general testers) do not offer an asymptotic advantage over simpler, parallel testing schemes.
